slots.title: August new home sales 0.68M beat 0.62M est.
slots.body:
August new home sales ran at a 0.68M annual pace — above the 0.62M estimate and July’s 0.64M.

That print landed the same week the 30-year fixed mortgage rate was reported at 7.5%, described as the highest since April 2024 as long-term bond yields moved up.

Housing demand in the data still moved up month over month even with those borrowing costs in the headlines.

What housing release do you watch first when rates and sales both shift?

slots.title: US close — Sept. 24, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished at 7,703.83, down 2.20 points (−0.0%) after trading between 7,662.57 and 7,719.01.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 161.61 points (−0.3%) to 51,349.98.

The Nasdaq Composite rose 3.34 points (0.0%) to 26,939.37, with a session low of 26,706.14.

The Russell 2000 slipped −0.1% to 2,835.57.

The VIX rose +3.2% to 15.67, up from a 15.18 prior close and as high as 16.57 intraday.

At 12:30 p.m.
ET, initial jobless claims for the week of Sep/19 printed 197K vs a 201K estimate (prior 198K).
Continuing claims were 1719K vs a 1750K estimate.
The four-week average was 202.25K.

At 2:00 p.m.
ET, August new home sales came in at 0.684M units vs a 0.620M estimate (previous 0.643M).

Communication Services led Nasdaq sectors at about +3.1%, paced by $META +4.5% to 777.59 (session high 779.82, matching the 52-week high in the data) and gains in $GOOGL (+1.3%) and $GOOG (+1.2%).

Healthcare averaged about +1.1%; $LLY rose +2.9% to 1,183.86.
Technology averaged about +0.9% while $NVDA ended −0.4% at 224.58 and $AVGO −1.3% at 350.36.

Consumer Defensive averaged about −1.7%: $WMT −2.7%, $PEP −1.6%, and $COST −0.9% after EPS of $6.75 vs $6.54 estimated and revenue of $93.87B vs $94.97B estimated.

$ORCL fell −3.5% to 139.53.
$SNX dropped −9.9% to 259.47 despite EPS of $5.68 vs $4.70 estimated and revenue above the estimate.
$DRI reported EPS of $2.05 on revenue of $3.20B vs $3.21B estimated and finished −2.9% at 207.44.

Energy lagged at about −1.3% on the Nasdaq sector read.
$XOM still closed +0.5% at 162.05.

In cross-assets, gold futures rose +0.5% to 4,319.10.
The United States Oil Fund ($USO proxy in the data) gained +2.9% to 153.09 while Brent crude was −1.1% at 105.47.
CNBC tied softer Brent to reporting on a potential diplomatic path related to Iran and navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund ($UUP) ticked +0.1% to 28.69.
Bitcoin ($BTCUSD) was −0.2% at 84,208.74.

The latest Treasury snapshot in the feed (dated 2026-09-22) shows the 10-year at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.25 percentage points.
